facts.text: After Shivaji Maharaj's death, the Marathas fought the Mughals under Sambhaji Maharaj, Rajaram Maharaj and Maharani Tarabai; this war of twenty seven years is called the 'Maratha War of Independence'.
facts.quote: the Marathas fought with great valour with the Mughals under the leadership of Chhatrapati Sambhaji Maharaj, Chhatrapati Rajaram Maharaj and Maharani Tarabai ... This long war that lasted for twenty seven years is called the 'Maratha War of Independence'.

facts.text: In 1682 CE Emperor Aurangzeb himself led the invasion of the South.
facts.quote: In 1682 CE Emperor Aurangzeb himself led the invasion of South.

facts.text: The word 'Maratha' here means 'people who speak Marathi' or 'Maharashtrian people'.
facts.quote: The word 'Maratha' used here means the 'people who speak Marathi' or 'Maharashtrian people'.

facts.text: Sambhaji Maharaj, the eldest son of Shivaji Maharaj, was born on 14 May 1657 on the Purandar Fort.
facts.quote: Sambhaji Maharaj was the eldest son of Chhatrapti Shivaji Maharaj. He was born on 14 May 1657 on the Purandar Fort.

facts.text: Aurangzeb's son Shahajada Akbar rebelled against his father and came to the Deccan to take shelter with Sambhaji Maharaj.
facts.quote: Emperor Aurangzeb's son Shahajada Akbar rebelled against his father. The Emperor crushed his rebellion. Then Akbar came to the Deccan to take shelter with Sambhaji Maharaj.

facts.text: Aurangzeb asked the Siddi of Janjira to undertake an expedition against the Marathas and won over the Portuguese to his side.
facts.quote: He asked the Siddi of Janjira to undertake an expedition against the Marathas. He also won over the Portuguese to his side.

facts.text: Sambhaji Maharaj began to take interest in administration and the command of the army from the age of fourteen years.
facts.quote: Sambhaji Maharaj had begun to take interst in the administration of the State and the command of the army from the age of fourteen years.

facts.text: French traveller Abbe Carrey said the young prince was courageous and brave like his father.
facts.quote: French traveller Abbe Carrey says about his battle skills, "Even though the prince is young, he is courageous and brave like his father was famous for...."

facts.text: Aurangzeb wanted to occupy regions from Kabul to Kannyakumari and create a grand unified Mughal empire.
facts.quote: Aurangzeb wanted to occupy regions from Kabul to Kannyakumari and create a grand unified Mughal empire.

facts.text: The Emperor's generals could not win the Maratha fort of Ramsej near Nashik; the siege continued for the next five years.
facts.quote: they couldn't win the Maratha fort of Ramsej near Nashik. ... So he put a siege around Ramsej fort near Nashik. ... The siege continued for the next five years.

facts.text: Aurangzeb once threw his turban on the floor and vowed not to wear it until he had vanquished Sambhaji.
facts.quote: Once he removed his turban in frustration and threw it on the floor. He made a vow that until he had vanquished Sambhaji, he would not wear his turban.

facts.text: Sabhasada described the Siddi of Janjira as a rat in the house.
facts.quote: Sabhasada has described him as a rat in the house.

facts.text: In 1682 CE Sambhaji Maharaj started a campaign against the Siddi; his army besieged Dandarajpuri fort and battered Janjira, but he turned back when the Mughal army invaded Swaraj.
facts.quote: Sambhaji Maharaj started a campaign against him in 1682 CE. His army laid a siege to Siddi's Dandarajpuri fort, and battered the fort of Janjira with the artillery. But at the same time, the Mughal army invaded Swaraj.

facts.text: Sambhaji Maharaj attacked the Revdanda fort of the Portuguese in 1683 CE.
facts.quote: He attacked the Revdanda fort of the Portuguese in 1683 CE.

facts.text: The Portuguese besieged the Maratha fort of Fonda; the Marathas broke through and attacked Goa, where Yesaji Kank showed great valour and the Portuguese Governor was wounded.
facts.quote: the Portuguese laid a siege to the Fonda fort of the Marathas on the Goa border. The Marathas broke through the siege and attacked Goa. In this battle, Yesaji Kank showed great valour. The Portuguese Governor got wounded and retreated.

facts.text: Sambhaji Maharaj abandoned the winning Goa campaign because the Mughals had attacked South Konkan.
facts.quote: Sambhaji Maharaj got the news that the Mughals had attacked South Konkan. Therefore, he had to abandon the winning campaign of Goa

facts.text: Aurangzeb suspended his campaign against the Marathas and conquered the kingdoms of Adilshah and Qutubshah.
facts.quote: Therefore, he suspended that campaign. Then he turned towards the kingdoms of Adilshah and Qutubshah and conquered them.

facts.text: Maratha General Hambirrao Mohite was killed in an encounter with the Mughal army.
facts.quote: The Maratha army General Hambirrao Mohite got killed during an encounter with the Mughal army.

facts.text: Sambhaji Maharaj gave administrative powers and her own stamp to Maharani Yesubai.
facts.quote: He gave administrative powers to Maharani Yesubai. He gave her, her own stamp.

facts.text: Sambhaji Maharaj composed 'Budhbhushanam' in Sanskrit; its second chapter discusses polity.
facts.quote: Sambhaji Maharaj composed 'Budhbhushanam' in the Sanskrit language. The second chapter of this book discusses polity.

facts.text: Mukarrabkhan, in charge of the Kolhapur province, raided Sangameshwar in Konkan and captured Sambhaji Maharaj.
facts.quote: He had placed Mukarrabkhan in charge of the Kolhapur province. Mukarrabkhan learnt that Sambhaji Maharaj was at Sangameshwar in Konkan. He raided the place and captured Sambhaji Maharaj.

facts.text: By the Emperor's orders, Sambhaji Maharaj was put to death on 11 March 1689.
facts.quote: By the Emperor's orders, he was brutally put to death on 11 March 1689.

facts.text: Rajaram Maharaj, the second son of Shivaji Maharaj, was born on 24 February 1670 on Raigad.
facts.quote: Rajaram Maharaj was the second son of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. He was born on 24 February 1670 on Raigad.

facts.text: Aurangzeb sent Zulfikarkhan to put Raigad under siege.
facts.quote: He sent Zulfikarkhan to put Raigad under siege.

facts.text: Maharani Yesubai chose to make Rajaram Maharaj, not her own son, the Chhatrapati; the defence of Raigad continued under her leadership.
facts.quote: It was decided that the fight to defend Raigad would continue under the leadership of Maharani Yesubai. Maharani Yesubai chose to make Rajaram Maharaj and not her own son the Chhatrapati.

facts.text: On 5 April 1689 Rajaram Maharaj escaped from the besieged Raigad and decided to go south to Jinji.
facts.quote: On 5 April 1689 Rajaram Maharaj escaped from the besieged Raigad with a few of his associates. He decided to go south to Jinji.

facts.text: Rajaram Maharaj reached Jinji with faithful Sardars like Pralhad Niraji, Khando Ballal and Rupaji Bhosale.
facts.quote: Rajaram Maharaj took his faithful Sardars like Pralhad Niraji, Khando Ballal, Rupaji Bhosale and managed to reach Jinji.

facts.text: The Mughals captured Raigad in November 1689 and arrested Maharani Yesubai and Shahu.
facts.quote: The Mughals captured Raigad in November 1689 and arrested Maharani Yesubai and Shahu.

facts.text: Rajaram Maharaj gave the duty of fighting the Mughals to Ramchandrapant Amatya, Shankaraji Narayan Sachiv, Santaji Ghorpade and Dhanaji Jadhav.
facts.quote: Rajaram Maharaj had assigned the duty to fight against the Mughals to Ramchandrapant Amatya, Shankaraji Narayan Sachiv, Santaji Ghorpade and Dhanaji Jadhav.

facts.text: It was promised that Mughal territory captured by a Maratha Sardar would be given to him as a jagir.
facts.quote: It was promised that if a Maratha Sardar captured Mughal territory it would be given to him as a jagir.

facts.text: Santaji Ghorpade and Vithoji Chavan cut and carried away the golden pinnacle of the Emperor's own tent.
facts.quote: Santaji Ghorpade and Vithoji Chavan even cut and carried away the golden pinnacle of the Emperor's own tent in a surprise attack.

facts.text: Zulfikarkhan besieged Jinji; the Marathas defended it for nearly eight years; Rajaram Maharaj escaped and later Zulfikarkhan captured Jinji.
facts.quote: He laid siege to the fort of Jinji. The Marathas defended the fort bravely for nearly eight years. ... Rajaram Maharaj escaped through the siege, and returned to Maharashtra. Later Zulfikarkhan captured the fort of Jinji.

facts.text: Mughal soldiers feared Dhanaji so much that when a horse baulked at water they asked, 'Why, do you see Dhanaji in the water?'
facts.quote: The Mughal soldiers were so scared of Dhanaji that when their horse baulked while drinking water, they would say: "Why, do you see Dhanaji in the water?"

facts.text: After Rajaram Maharaj returned, the Marathas attacked the Mughal territories of Khandesh, Varhad and Baglan.
facts.quote: The Marathas attacked the Mughal territories of Khandesh, Varhad and Baglan.

facts.text: Rajaram Maharaj died on 2 March 1700 on Sinhgad after a short illness.
facts.quote: Rajaram Maharaj died on 2 March 1700 on Sinhgad after a short period of illness.

facts.text: Rajaram Maharaj fought Aurangzeb for 11 years; historian Riyasatkar G. S. Sardesai called him 'Sthirbuddhi' (Level Headed).
facts.quote: he fought against Aurangzeb for 11 years ... noted historian Riyasatkar G. S. Sardesai has used the adjective 'Sthirbuddhi' (Level Headed).

facts.text: Mughal historian Khafikhan described Maharani Tarabai as an intelligent and knowledgeable woman.
facts.quote: Contemporary Mughal historian Khafikhan describes Maharani Tarabai as an intelligent and knowledgeable woman.

facts.text: Aurangzeb captured Satara and Panhala, while the Marathas dashed up to Mughal areas of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat.
facts.quote: Aurangzeb captured Satara and Panhala from the Maratha territory, but at the same time the Marathas dashed up to the Mughal areas of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat.

facts.text: Sardars Krishnaji Sawant, Khanderao Dabhade, Dhanaji Jadhav and Nemaji Shinde opened battles against the Mughals outside Maharashtra.
facts.quote: Sardars like Krishnaji Sawant, Khanderao Dabhade, Dhanaji Jadhav and Nemaji Shinde opened battles against Mughals on various fronts outside Maharashtra.

facts.text: Maharani Tarabai fought for seven years; Maratha Sardars fought the Mughals up to Sironje, Mandsaur and Malwa.
facts.quote: Maharani Tarabai fought for seven years. ... Maratha Sardars fought against the Mughals up to Sironje, Mandsaur and Malwa.

facts.text: Tarabai's 'Safe deposit locker system': a Killedar handed a fort to Aurangzeb for a bribe, deposited it in the Maratha treasury, and Tarabai later recaptured the restocked fort.
facts.quote: A bribe was accepted from Aurangzeb and the fort was handed over to him. The Killedar used to deposit this bribe amount in the Maratha treasury. ... Tarabai used to capture that fort again. This strategy of Tarabai is described as 'Safe deposit locker system'.

facts.text: Poet Devdatta, son of Paramanand (author of Shivbharat), described Tarabai's great achievements.
facts.quote: While describing Tarabai's great achievements, Poet Devdatta (who was the son of Paramanand, the author or Shivbharat) says,

facts.text: After 25 years of Mughal-Maratha fighting, Emperor Aurangzeb died in 1707 CE at Ahmednagar; the Maratha War of Independence ended with his death.
facts.quote: The Mughal-Maratha fight had continued for 25 years. ... Emperor Aurangzeb died in 1707 CE at Ahmednagar. The Maratha War of Independence ended with his death.

facts.text: The Marathas controlled the throne of Delhi and ran the affairs of almost all parts of Hindusthan, so the 18th century is known as the century of the Marathas.
facts.quote: They controlled the throne of Delhi, ran the affairs of almost all parts of Hindusthan and protected it. Therefore, the 18th century is known as the century of the Marathas.

facts.text: In the family tree of the Bhonsales, Malojiraje is followed by Shahajiraje (1594 CE to 1664 CE), whose sons are Sambhaji, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and Vyankoji.
facts.quote: Malojiraje ... Shahajiraje (1594 CE to 1664 CE) ... Sambhaji | Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj (1630 CE to 1680 CE) | Vyankoji

facts.text: In the family tree, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj's dates are 1630 CE to 1680 CE.
facts.quote: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj (1630 CE to 1680 CE)

facts.text: In the family tree, Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj (1682 CE to 1749 CE) follows Sambhaji Maharaj, and Chhatrapati Ramraja (Adopted, 1750 CE to 1777 CE) follows Shahu.
facts.quote: Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj (1682 CE to 1749 CE) ... Chhatrapati Ramraja (Adopted 1750 CE to 1777 CE)

facts.text: Rajaram Maharaj's sons in the family tree are Chhatrapati Shivaji (son of Tarabai) and Chhatrapati Sambhaji (son of Rajasbai).
facts.quote: Chhatrapati Shivaji (Son of Tarabai) | Chhatrapati Sambhaji (Son of Rajasbai)
